title: What is Shasha?
display: This is Shasha: a calm YouTube for the family TV. No ads, and no need to sign in. And it comes with what reassures you about your children: their own profiles, a daily time limit, and a remote on your phone.
tts: This is Shasha: a calm YouTube for the family TV. No ads, and no need to sign in. And it comes with what reassures you about your children: their own profiles, a daily time limit, and a remote on your phone.

title: Why?
display: The idea is simple: calm, deliberate viewing. You watch what you chose, then turn the TV off feeling good, instead of losing an hour to a video you never looked for.
tts: The idea is simple: calm, deliberate viewing. You watch what you chose, then turn the TV off feeling good, instead of losing an hour to a video you never looked for.

title: Home
display: You open the app and find the latest from the channels you picked, newest first. Nothing is pushed at you, and nothing drags you from one video to the next.
tts: You open the app and find the latest from the channels you picked, newest first. Nothing is pushed at you, and nothing drags you from one video to the next.

title: Profiles: adults and children
display: Everyone in the family has their own profile. The adults' profile is protected by a secret code. A child's profile shows only the channels you allow, and it can only be left with the parents' code.
tts: Everyone in the family has their own profile. The adults' profile is protected by a secret code. A child's profile shows only the channels you allow, and it can only be left with the parents' code.

title: Time limits and hours
display: Each profile has a daily limit, and allowed viewing hours. Five minutes before the end, a small, gentle reminder appears. Then a "Time is up" screen, which opens only with the code.
tts: Each profile has a daily limit, and allowed viewing hours. Five minutes before the end, a small, gentle reminder appears. Then a Time is up screen, which opens only with the code.

title: Serious mode
display: Then there is "Serious mode": a video that has started does not stop before its end. Children and adults each have their own switch. A child leaves only with the parents' code. An adult needs a long press, then a sentence to type.
tts: Then there is Serious mode: a video that has started does not stop before its end. Children and adults each have their own switch. A child leaves only with the parents' code. An adult needs a long press, then a sentence to type.

title: The Guard
display: And if a child presses the Home button on the remote, the Guard covers the other app, and brings Shasha back within moments.
tts: And if a child presses the Home button on the remote, the Guard covers the other app, and brings Shasha back within moments.

title: Suggestions and Shorts
display: Suggested videos, and the short "Shorts" clips, can be shown or hidden for each profile separately. So your child's screen stays calm, and you keep what you like.
tts: Suggested videos, and the short Shorts clips, can be shown or hidden for each profile separately. So your child's screen stays calm, and you keep what you like.

title: Channel page
display: Every channel page is divided into sections: videos, Shorts, live streams, and playlists. And you choose the order: newest first, most viewed, or oldest.
tts: Every channel page is divided into sections: videos, Shorts, live streams, and playlists. And you choose the order: newest first, most viewed, or oldest.

title: Voice search
display: To search, press the microphone button and say what you want, in Arabic or in English. The results appear in moments.
tts: To search, press the microphone button and say what you want, in Arabic or in English. The results appear in moments.

title: The phone as a remote
display: Your phone becomes a remote: scan the QR code, to search, to control playback, and to send links. And in the "Parent" section, with the parents' code, you add time and manage a child's list.
tts: Your phone becomes a remote: scan the Q R code, to search, to control playback, and to send links. And in the Parent section, with the parents' code, you add time and manage a child's list.

title: Accept or decline
display: If someone sends a video from their phone, the TV asks you: "Accept" or "Decline". And what you are watching carries on until you decide.
tts: If someone sends a video from their phone, the TV asks you: Accept or Decline. And what you are watching carries on until you decide.

title: One-button updates
display: When a new version is released, press one button in Settings, and the download and installation start by themselves. No computer, and no reinstalling.
tts: When a new version is released, press one button in Settings, and the download and installation start by themselves. No computer, and no reinstalling.

title: Which TV?
display: Which TVs does Shasha run on? Every TV with Google TV or Android TV, and Amazon Fire TV devices.
tts: Which TVs does Shasha run on? Every TV with Google TV or Android TV, and Amazon Fire TV devices.

title: Samsung, LG and others
display: For a Samsung or LG TV, or any other, a small Android TV stick is enough. You plug it into the HDMI port, and Shasha runs on it with all its features.
tts: For a Samsung or L G TV, or any other, a small Android TV stick is enough. You plug it into the H D M I port, and Shasha runs on it with all its features.

title: Installing: what you need
display: Now the installation, step by step. You need a personal computer, a Mac or Windows, on the same network as the TV.
tts: Now the installation, step by step. You need a personal computer, a Mac or Windows, on the same network as the TV.

title: Step 1: Download
display: Step one, on the computer: from the Shasha page on GitHub, click the zip file "Shasha-Setup.zip", then the download button. Then unzip it: on Windows, right-click, then "Extract All". On a Mac, double-click.
tts: Step one, on the computer: from the Shasha page on GitHub, click the zip file, then the download button. Then unzip it: on Windows, right-click, then Extract All. On a Mac, double-click.

title: Step 2: Developer options
display: Step two, on the TV: open Settings, then System, then About. Scroll down to "Android TV OS build", and press the middle button seven times, until a message appears: "You are now a developer".
tts: Step two, on the TV: open Settings, then System, then About. Scroll down to Android TV O S build, and press the middle button seven times, until a message appears: You are now a developer.

title: Step 3: USB debugging
display: Step three: go back to System, and open Developer options. Turn on "USB debugging", and "Network debugging" if you see it.
tts: Step three: go back to System, and open Developer options. Turn on U S B debugging, and Network debugging if you see it.

title: Step 4: The TV's address
display: Step four: in Settings, open "Network & Internet". On Wi-Fi, choose your network, then "IP address". On a cable, the address is right under "Ethernet". Write it down: numbers with dots between them.
tts: Step four: in Settings, open Network and Internet. On Wi-Fi, choose your network, then I P address. On a cable, the address is right under Ethernet. Write it down: numbers with dots between them.

title: Step 5: Run on Windows
display: Step five, on the computer: on Windows, double-click the Windows file. If a blue warning appears, choose "More info", then "Run anyway".
tts: Step five, on the computer: on Windows, double-click the Windows file. If a blue warning appears, choose More info, then Run anyway.

title: Step 5: Run on a Mac
display: On a Mac, double-click the Mac file. If the Mac refuses to open it, open "System Settings", then "Privacy & Security", then "Open Anyway".
tts: On a Mac, double-click the Mac file. If the Mac refuses to open it, open System Settings, then Privacy and Security, then Open Anyway.

title: Step 5: Type the address
display: The program will ask: "Enter the TV's IP address". Type the address you wrote down, then press Enter.
tts: The program will ask: Enter the TV's I P address. Type the address you wrote down, then press Enter.

title: Step 6: Allow
display: Step six, on the TV: a message will ask whether to allow debugging. Tick "Always allow from this computer", then press "OK" within a minute.
tts: Step six, on the TV: a message will ask whether to allow debugging. Tick Always allow from this computer, then press Okay within a minute.

title: Step 7: The program finishes by itself
display: Step seven: the program finishes by itself. It installs the app, gives it its permissions, then asks whether to stop the official YouTube app. Type the letter Y to agree, or N to decline. Then it shows a summary.
tts: Step seven: the program finishes by itself. It installs the app, gives it its permissions, then asks whether to stop the official YouTube app. Type the letter Y to agree, or N to decline. Then it shows a summary.

title: Step 8: First start
display: Step eight: the first start. Choose the parents' code, then create your own profile, and your child's profile with their daily minutes and allowed hours. Then add the channels you allow.
tts: Step eight: the first start. Choose the parents' code, then create your own profile, and your child's profile with their daily minutes and allowed hours. Then add the channels you allow.

title: The phone app
display: And there is a Shasha app for your Android phone too, with its own video that explains it.
tts: And there is a Shasha app for your Android phone too, with its own video that explains it.

title: Closing
display: And that is Shasha. Made with love for my family. Ahmad Nayfeh.
tts: And that is Shasha. Made with love for my family. Ahmad Nayfeh.
